en.title: Interjections and particles
en.summary: An interjection shows a sudden feeling, and a particle is a small word with a purely grammatical job.

paragraphs: An interjection shows a sudden feeling or a reaction, and it stands outside the grammar of the sentence. A particle is a small word that does a grammatical job but does not fit the other classes well. Both are short, and both are very common in speech.

The to of an infinitive and the not of a negative are often called particles. An interjection is followed by an exclamation mark or a comma, and it can stand alone as a sentence. It never changes its form and has no other word depending on it.

blocks.html:
WordJob
to (to swim)marks the infinitive
notmakes the verb negative
oh, hey, hellointerjections
well, so, you knowdiscourse markers in speech
yes, noanswer words

paragraphs: Words such as well, so and anyway have little meaning of their own. They organise a conversation: they start a turn, change topic or show hesitation. Writers use them less than speakers.
Many interjections imitate a sound or a feeling: ah, oh, hmm, ugh, ouch. Their spelling is not fixed. The same sound may appear as ah or aah, and each community writes them slightly differently.

items: Wrong: **I want swim.** Right: **I want to swim.**
Wrong: **Well I think so.** Right: **Well, I think so.**
Wrong: **I not know.** Right: **I do not know.**

ro.title: Interjecțiile și particulele
ro.summary: Interjecțiile exprimă emoții și sunete, iar particulele sunt cuvinte scurte cu rol gramatical.

paragraphs: Interjecția este un cuvânt scurt care exprimă o stare, o reacție sau un sunet. Ea nu se schimbă și nu depinde de alte cuvinte din propoziție. Particula este un cuvânt mic cu rol gramatical precis.
Interjecțiile sunt urmate adesea de semnul exclamării sau de virgulă. Particulele stau de obicei lângă verbe și nu își schimbă forma. De exemplu, particula „să” ajută la formarea modului conjunctiv.
